newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: North Star Vietnam merger plan lapses.
newsitem.headline: North Star Vietnam merger plan lapses.

text.p: North Star Resources NL said on Wednesday that an agreement with financier Robert Friedland's Indochina Resources Ltd to combine both companies' Vietnam minerals resource assets has not been concluded.
"The conditions have not been completed in the time limit under the agreement and hence the contract has now lapsed," North Star said in a statement to the Australian Stock Exchange.

The agreement was subject to independent valuations of mineral projects in Vietnam held by both companies, it said. Edward Flood, president of Indochina Goldfields, said the two sides failed to find the needed synergy to complete the deal.
Flood said the merger of assets with North Star was one of several deals Indochina is looking at in Vietnam and that there would be no material impact on Indochina's overall opeations.

Indochina Goldfields listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange earlier this year after raising C$270 million to fund efforts to establish a far-reaching mining company operating in Southeast Asia. Friedland, the founder of Diamond Fields Resources Inc, which discovered the giant Voisey's Bay nickel deposit in Canada, is chairman of Singapore-based Indochina Goldfields.

The agreement would have combined all of Indochina Goldfields' mineral resource assets in Vietnam, which includes its investment and mining license for the the Bong Mieu gold mining project and other large exploration acreage with the Sin Quyen copper and gold project, owned by North Star, according to earlier statements to the Australian Stock Exchange.
The assets were to be bundled into a new company called Newco, which North Star said would seek a listing on a Canadian stock exchange.
North Star officials were not available for comment.
